profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA, and is currently led by Ali Farhadi. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, with work spanning climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife and ecosystem protection. Its research is guided by principles around openness, collaboration, and inclusivity, with the stated goal of producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems.

Ai2's notable products include OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs. The organization partners with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering on foundational and applied research, with the NSF on the Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure to Accelerate Science project, and with Google Cloud on the development of open AI models and platforms for scientific research and environmental modeling.

The held facts confirm Ai2 is a verified nonprofit research lab with no litigation or MCP server presence on record.
